message.content:
Here’s a quick, step‑by‑step guide on how to pull the CNAME records for **`sample.com`** via the VirusTotal API and then isolate just the related object IDs. --- ## 1. Make the API Call ### Using `curl` ```bash curl -X GET \ -H "x-apikey: secret123" \ "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/records?record_type=CNAME" ``` > **Tip:** > *If you’re using a different programming language, just replace the `curl` line with the equivalent HTTP GET request, ensuring you set the `x-apikey` header to your key (`secret123`).* --- ## 2. Understand the Response Structure A successful request returns JSON similar to: ```json { "data": [ { "id": "CNAME_123456", "attributes": { ... } }, { "id": "CNAME_789012", "attributes": { ... } } ], "meta": { ... } } ``` - The top‑level key is `"data"`. - Each element inside `"data"` represents one CNAME record. - Every record contains an `"id"` field – that’s the unique identifier you’re after. --- ## 3. Extract Only the IDs Below are snippets in a few common languages that pull out just the IDs. | Language | Code | |----------|------| | **Python (requests)** | ```python
import requests, json
headers = {"x-apikey": "secret123"}
resp = requests.get("https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/records?record_type=CNAME", headers=headers)
ids = [item["id"] for item in resp.json()["data"]]
print(ids)``` | | **JavaScript (fetch)** | ```js
const headers = new Headers({ "x-apikey": "secret123" });
fetch("https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/records?record_type=CNAME", { headers })
.then(r => r.json())
.then(json => console.log(json.data.map(item => item.id)));``` | | **Bash (jq)** | ```bash
curl -s -H "x-apikey: secret123" "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/records?record_type=CNAME" \\\n | jq -r '.data[].id'``` | > **Result:** > A plain list of IDs, e.g. `["CNAME_123456","CNAME_789012"]`. --- ## 4. What to Do With Those IDs Once you have the IDs, you can: - Query each ID directly: `GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/records/` - Use them in bulk queries or for further analysis. --- ### Quick Recap 1. **Call** the endpoint with your API key in the `x-apikey` header. 2. **Parse** the JSON; look under `"data"`. 3. **Map** each entry to its `"id"` field. That’s all you need to retrieve and isolate the CNAME record IDs for `sample.com`. Happy querying!
